name: VWO
summary: A/B testing and conversion optimization platform. Run experiments, heatmaps and personalization to lift conversions without developers.
best_for: teams that want an all-in-one experience-optimisation platform (A/B testing + heatmaps + personalisation) with friendlier Bayesian stats and transparent pricing
skip_if: you're a small business wanting advanced targeting/MVT on the entry tier (you'll be priced up), or an enterprise running massive concurrent experiments — Optimizely handles that scale
honest_knock: The jump from Growth to Pro is steep — small businesses get priced out of MVT and complex targeting — and the UI is dense with options. Some users note the reporting breaks more often than pricier tools (though it doesn't affect the tests themselves). The part that costs people money later is what happens to a winner. VWO applies page changes through its SmartCode — their own page says the asynchronous SmartCode “loads page changes asynchronously when the web page loads” — so a variant left running in the editor is rendered by VWO rather than built into your site. Fine while you pay, gone when you stop. Their server-side testing changes the arithmetic here, because those changes live in your own stack; the client-side ones do not.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: No price is published any more, and the site has moved. Re-read on 20 September 2026: vwo.com now answers HTTP 301 and redirects to wingify.com — vwo.com/pricing/ to wingify.com/pricing/, vwo.com/free-trial/ to wingify.com/free-trial/ — and the pricing page is titled "Pricing & Plans | Wingify Platform", with the products named Wingify Testing, Wingify Personalization and Wingify Insights and a site-wide banner announcing that AB Tasty and VWO have united. The tier structure is unchanged: Growth, Pro and Enterprise as feature tables only, every button a Schedule a Demo, no currency amount anywhere in the rendered page and none in wingify.com/llms.txt either — the same picture as the 4 and 10 September 2026 readings. The ~$314/mo for 10k MTUs this dossier carried until 4 September 2026 was a published figure the vendor has since withdrawn. Two things are new on the page. A per-MAU meter is now visible in the comparison table — 50, 100 and 200 events stored per MAU across the tiers — under the vendor's own footnote that the limit is not implemented in the app, is representational, does not affect current pricing and will apply in future to all customers on their respective plans. And API access at Enterprise is now listed with a rate limit of 60K a month. Wandz, the AI layer the 10 September reading found sold in Core and Advanced tiers, is no longer named on the pricing page. The tier lines are unchanged: multivariate testing, guardrail metrics, advanced targeting and downloadable reports start at Pro; API access, SSO, mutually exclusive groups and a dedicated CSM only at Enterprise.
